docs_meta_description: How the Gestura exchange format works: menus, search engines, fields and validation rules.
docs_intro: Gestura menus and search engines can be exported, shared and imported as portable JSON files. This index stores and distributes them, but the format itself does not depend on it: the browser extension can import and export these files directly, with no server involved.
docs_optional_note: The extension works entirely without this index. Sharing here is an optional, free add-on — nothing in the extension depends on this backend being reachable.
docs_menu_body: A menu file has the marker "gesturaMenu": 1 at the top level and describes an in-page menu: a list of items (links, searches or actions such as scrolling and navigation) that appears on matching websites. Each item needs a unique id; a non-separator item must use one of a fixed set of allowed actions.
docs_engine_body: An engine file has the marker "gesturaEngine": 1 and describes a single custom search engine or quick link: a name, an https url template, and optional settings such as result formatting or other behaviour flags. An engine may include transformCode, a small JavaScript snippet that reshapes the search result before it is used.
docs_fields_body: Every entry has an id (a short, reverse-domain-style identifier, e.g. example.com.my-menu) and a version following semantic versioning (major.minor.patch, e.g. 1.2.0). name and, where present, description accept either a plain string or an object keyed by language code, such as an "en" entry alongside a "de" entry, with English used as the fallback when a viewer's language is missing. Menus use patterns (URL match patterns) and items; engines use a url template instead.
docs_rules_body: The server validates every submission with the same rules the extension itself enforces: all URLs (homepage, item links, engine url) must start with https:; ids, names, descriptions and URLs are limited in length; a menu holds at most 100 items and at most 50 patterns; item ids must be unique within a menu; a searchLink item needs either an engineId or a url. Entries that contain transformCode always go through manual moderation before publication, since executable code needs a human look.
about_meta_description: What the Gestura Index is: an optional, free add-on for sharing Gestura menus and search engines, and how it relates to the extension.
about_can_share_body: Browse, download, and import other people's menus and search engines — or publish your own. No account, no sign-up.
about_can_updates_body: Gestura can ask anonymously whether newer versions of your installed menus and search engines exist — with no identifier, and without the index learning who is asking.
about_can_sync_body: If you use Gestura on several devices, you can sync your settings. Encryption happens on your device: the index stores unreadable ciphertext only and knows neither the key nor the identifier behind it.
about_prepared_note: Complete on the server — available with the upcoming version of the extension.
about_privacy_body: No account, no e-mail, no IP addresses. Downloads are counted as an anonymous number only. For settings sync, the index sees encrypted data exclusively — and stores the identifier it lives under as a checksum only.
about_intro: Gestura Index is a free, optional service for sharing Gestura menus and search engines — website menus, quick searches and links that Gestura users configure and want to share with others.
about_relation_body: The Gestura browser extension works entirely on its own. Nothing in the extension depends on this index being reachable: menus and engines can always be exported and imported directly as files, with no server involved. This site only adds a convenient way to discover and share them.
about_optional_body: Using the index is entirely optional and free of charge. There is no obligation to submit anything here, and browsing, searching and downloading entries requires no account.
about_source_body: Gestura Index is open source. The backend, frontend, and the shared exchange-format schema all live in one public repository.
about_license_body: The project is licensed under the AGPL-3.0-or-later.
privacy_meta_description: Privacy policy for the Gestura Index: what data is processed, on what legal basis, how long it is kept — and what rights you have.
privacy_intro: The Gestura Index is built for data minimisation: as little as possible is collected — only what running the service actually requires. This policy describes each processing activity individually, with its legal basis and retention period.
privacy_pill: Data minimisation by design · Last updated: September 2026
privacy_fact_tracking: No trackers, no analytics, no advertising
privacy_fact_account: No account, no email address, no password
privacy_fact_ip: IP addresses are not stored permanently
privacy_fact_e2e: Settings encrypted end-to-end — we cannot read them
privacy_fact_eu: No third-party servers, no data outside the EU
privacy_controller_body: The controller responsible for data processing on this website is Patric Pesch, Sülzgürtel 64, 50937 Köln, Germany, contact@gestura.eu. No data protection officer has been appointed; the statutory conditions requiring one are not met.
privacy_logs_body: When you open a page, your browser transmits technically necessary data to the server — including your IP address, date and time, the requested address, the status code and the amount of data transferred. These logs are created by the hosting provider; they serve operations and attack mitigation only, are not combined with other data and are not evaluated for statistics or analytics. The legal basis is the legitimate interest in a functioning, secure service (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). The provider deletes these logs automatically after a short period.
privacy_retention_logs: deleted by the provider after a short period
privacy_storage_body: No cookies are set. Three items are kept in your browser's local storage so the site behaves the way you operate it:
privacy_storage_theme: Your choice between the light and dark appearance.
privacy_storage_basket: The identifiers of the entries you added to your selection. This list leaves your device only when you explicitly hand the selection over to the extension.
privacy_storage_pages: Which information pages are currently visible, so the navigation does not flicker briefly on your next visit.
privacy_storage_legal: All three are strictly necessary for the service you explicitly requested and therefore exempt from consent under § 25(2)(2) TDDDG — which is why there is no consent banner here. None of them contains an identifier that could recognise your device, none is transmitted to the server, and all can be deleted at any time through your browser settings. The language choice lives in the page address (/de, /en) and is not stored at all.
privacy_retention_storage: until you clear your browser's local storage
privacy_abuse_body: Write access to the API is rate-limited so that individual senders cannot overload the service or distort ratings and reports. For this, your IP address is counted briefly in a cache — not in the database, with no link to content, and only for the duration of the respective window (15 minutes to 24 hours depending on the operation). The entry then expires by itself. The legal basis is the legitimate interest in preventing abuse (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
privacy_submit_body: When you submit a menu or search engine you receive a secret edit token that is stored in your own browser only. The server keeps just a hash of it (Argon2id) — the token itself is never stored and cannot be derived from the hash. This lets you update or delete your entry later without creating an account, without an email address and without a password. The legal basis is performance of the usage relationship (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR). If you lose the token you lose access to the entry; there is no recovery path, because we hold nothing that would let us identify you.
privacy_public_content_body: Menus and search engines that are submitted are by their nature meant to be browsed and downloaded by others — that is the purpose of the index. Only submit content you are willing to share publicly; do not include personal data in names, descriptions or URLs. Optional screenshots for an entry are re-encoded server-side and stored without metadata; third-party URLs are never embedded.
privacy_counters_body: Downloads increment an anonymous, aggregated install counter per entry. This counter cannot be traced back to a person, a device or an IP address — it is a plain number, not a record of who downloaded what.
privacy_reports_body: Reports about an entry are processed anonymously: only the reported entry, the reason, an optional comment and the timestamp are stored — no identifier of the reporting person and no IP address. The legal basis is the legitimate interest in keeping the directory free of abuse (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
privacy_accounts_body: An account is not required to use the index; it is pure convenience. An account consists solely of a random access token — of which only a short selector and a hash (Argon2id) are stored, plus the times of creation and last access. There is no email address, no name, no password and no profile. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR. Accounts unused for 365 days are deleted automatically along with all associated data.
privacy_ratings_body: With an account you can leave one star rating with an optional comment per entry. The rating, the comment and the timestamp are stored, linked to the account, so that you can change or withdraw your own rating. Comments are publicly visible; do not write anything there that could identify you. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR.
privacy_sync_body: If you want to synchronise your Gestura settings across several browsers, you can transfer them through this service. Synchronisation is a second switch, independent of the general integration and with a confirmation of its own — enabling the integration does not by itself synchronise anything. The data is encrypted on your device alone and reaches the server as ciphertext only; the key never leaves your device. We can neither read nor merge the contents — merging is done by the extension. Synchronisation is addressed via an identifier derived from your secret, which is stored server-side only as a SHA-256 hash; the identifier itself is not stored and request bodies are not logged. What is stored is the ciphertext, its checksum and size, and the times of last modification. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR. States not accessed for 365 days are deleted automatically.
privacy_updates_body: The Gestura extension can ask the index whether newer versions of the installed menus and search engines exist. In doing so it transmits their identifiers and version numbers — with no account, no device identifier and no user identifier. The request is answered and not stored. This connection does not arise by itself: the gestura.eu integration is switched off by default in the extension and takes effect only after you have explicitly confirmed it; if its scope is extended later, the extension asks again. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR.
privacy_admin_body: Moderation happens in a closed administration area. It stores the name and email address of the administrating persons, their passkeys (public keys, no biometric data) and a log of administrative actions — the latter to keep decisions accountable. A cookie is set only in this area: a strictly necessary session cookie that ends when the browser is closed and is never set for visitors. Invitations to the administration area are sent by email via the hosting provider's mail server. The legal bases are Art. 6(1)(b) and (f) GDPR.
privacy_recipients_body: The website and API are operated at ALL-INKL.COM – Neue Medien Münnich, Hauptstraße 68, 02742 Friedersdorf, Germany, which also holds the server logs and handles mail delivery. A data processing agreement under Art. 28 GDPR is in place with this provider. There are no other recipients: no analytics or advertising services, no social networks, no external fonts and no content delivery networks. The pages load no resources from third-party servers.
privacy_thirdcountry_body: No personal data is transferred to countries outside the European Union. Servers and processors are located in Germany.
privacy_rights_intro: You have the following rights vis-à-vis the controller:
privacy_rights_access: Access to the data stored about you (Art. 15 GDPR)
privacy_rights_object: Objection to processing based on legitimate interests (Art. 21 GDPR)
privacy_rights_anonymous: One point matters especially here: because the service deliberately works without identification, we cannot attribute most data to a person. For an anonymous account, an edit token or a synchronisation state we can only respond if you present the corresponding token — without it we are neither obliged nor able to keep additional data for the sole purpose of identifying you (Art. 11 GDPR). This is not an evasion but the flip side of data minimisation: what we do not hold cannot be disclosed or misused either.
privacy_rights_contact: To exercise your rights, an informal message to contact@gestura.eu is sufficient.
privacy_complaint_body: Without prejudice to other remedies, you have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (Art. 77 GDPR). The competent authority is the Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information of North Rhine-Westphalia, Kavalleriestraße 2–4, 40213 Düsseldorf, Germany. You may also contact the supervisory authority where you habitually reside.
privacy_no_profiling_body: There is no automated decision-making, including profiling, within the meaning of Art. 22 GDPR. Providing data is neither legally nor contractually required; without the details described above, however, the respective function cannot be used.
privacy_changes_body: This policy is updated whenever the processing activities described here change — for example when new features are added. The version in force is always available on this page.

c1_page_title: Gestura — mouse gestures for your browser
c1_meta_desc: Mouse gestures, super-drag, wheel and rocker gestures, and area selection — with custom search engines and website menus. Anonymous, no account, open source.
c1_status_pill: Open source · AGPL · Chrome, Edge & Firefox
c1_hero_h1_a: The fastest way through your web
c1_hero_sub: Mouse gestures, super-drag, wheel and rocker gestures, area selection — plus your own search engines and website menus. No account, no tracking, no compromises.
c1_feat_gestures_title: Mouse gestures with a visible trail
c1_feat_gestures_body: Hold the right button, draw a stroke — Gestura draws along and shows the recognized action live. Every sequence of directions is freely assignable.
c1_feat_superdrag_body: Drag links, text or images — the direction decides the action: open, search, save.
c1_feat_wheel_body: Wheel with a button held, or both buttons alternating — switch tabs without looking.
c1_feat_area_body: Drag a rectangle, then open or copy every link inside it.
c1_feat_engines_body: Every website with a search box becomes a search engine — select, gesture, result.
c1_feat_menus_body: Your own context menus per website — shareable through the Gestura Index.
c1_teaser_heading: Don't start from scratch: ready-made menus & search engines.
c2_meta_desc: What Gestura is and does: mouse gestures, super-drag, wheel and rocker gestures, and area selection — usable anonymously, no account, open source (AGPL).
c2_intro: Gestura is a free browser extension for Chrome, Edge, and Firefox that controls your browser through movement: mouse gestures, super-drag, wheel and rocker gestures, and area selection. Instead of toolbar buttons and nested menus, a short hand movement is enough — go back, go forward, open a tab, start a search. Everything runs locally in your browser: no account, no e-mail, no tracking data. The source code is open (AGPL).
c2_persona_surf_body: If you juggle dozens of tabs every day, gestures save you hundreds of clicks.
c2_persona_research_body: Select text and look it up in your search engine of choice with a single gesture — no detour.
c2_persona_privacy_body: No data collection, no account, open code — verifiable on GitHub.
c2_sec_gestures_body: Hold the right mouse button and draw a line — Gestura visibly traces the path and shows the recognized action in the middle of the screen. Every direction sequence can be freely assigned, and the trail's color and width are configurable.
c2_sec_engines_body: Any website with a search field can be set up as a search engine. Select text, run the gesture, get the result in a new tab. Find ready-made collections in the Gestura Index — or share your own.
c2_sec_engines_link: Discover search engines in the index
c2_sec_menus_body: Custom context menus per website: the most important actions and destinations appear right where you're working. Menus are shareable — as a JSON export or through the Index.
c2_privacy_banner_title: Data minimalism from the ground up.
c2_privacy_banner_body: Gestura sends no usage data, stores no IP addresses, and requires no account. The Gestura Index is anonymous to use too. The entire codebase is AGPL-licensed and on GitHub.
c3_meta_desc: What a mouse gesture is and how it works: a direction or sequence of directions while holding the right mouse button – with eight examples, freely reassignable in Gestura.
c3_intro: A mouse gesture is a short stroke while holding the right mouse button. The direction – or a sequence of directions – triggers an action. After a few minutes the movements sit in muscle memory: you think "back" and your hand does it.
c3_footnote: All mappings are examples – in Gestura every gesture is freely assignable.
c4_meta_desc: Gestura compared with other gesture extensions: consistent privacy, Firefox support, and an open, shareable index for menus and search engines.
c4_intro: There are many gesture extensions out there. What sets Gestura apart: consistent privacy, Firefox support, and an open, shareable index for menus and search engines.
